h1: Register a child as a British citizen
intro: Many children can register as British citizens, depending on where they were born and their parents’ status. We work out whether you can register a child as a British citizen as of right, or under the Home Office’s discretion.
cardText: Children born in the UK or with British or settled parents.

rules.title: Already British?
rules.text: Children born in the UK to a British or settled parent are usually British already, and just need a passport.

rules.title: Apply before 18
rules.text: Most registration routes for children must be applied for before their 18th birthday.

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: How to register a child as a British citizen
sections.text: The route depends on the child’s birthplace, the parents’ status at the time of birth and since, and how long the child has lived in the UK. We look at your family’s history and tell you which route applies.

faqs.q: Is my UK-born child already British?
faqs.a: If a parent was British or settled when the child was born, usually yes.

faqs.q: Can I register a child born abroad?
faqs.a: Sometimes, depending on the parents’ status. We check.

faqs.q: Does my child need to take the Life in the UK test?
